events.text:
**Recommendation:** Expect slow pier fishing at all four ports this week. If you go, I'd pick St. Joseph. Its pier heads were the only place where reports showed salmon near the structure. The newest reports are 6 days old (2022-09-14).

| Port | Pier rating (0–4) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph | 1 (below average) | Salmon were near the pier heads, but only a few were caught. |
| South Haven | 1 (below average) | There's no recent pier report, so this is a low-confidence guess. |
| Grand Haven | 0 (slow) | The last two pier reports both said slow. |
| Muskegon | 0 (slow) | No salmon were reported from the breakwalls, and there's no pier report since. |

**What the reports say**
- **St. Joseph:** "A couple of boats fishing the pier heads" caught a couple of coho and Chinook (St. Joseph, 2022-09-14). That was boat fishing at the pier heads, not pier fishing. The latest actual pier report is from 2022-08-17. It said a few Chinook were caught but it was mostly steelhead, and the salmon that were caught took spoons and spinners (St. Joseph, 2022-08-17). On 2022-08-24, "a few fish around the piers" was still rated slow (St. Joseph, 2022-08-24).
- **South Haven:** There are no pier-specific salmon reports in the window. Boat fishing was "decent when they could get out," with a mix of Chinook, coho and steelhead on spoons in about 110 ft of water (South Haven, 2022-09-14). The piers were closed to fishing for several days because of red-flag lake conditions (South Haven, 2022-08-10). Check for closures before you drive.
- **Grand Haven:** "The pier action was slow for salmon" (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-07). The boats are doing better, at 55–110 ft down in 120–210 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14). The fish are well offshore, not at the pier.
- **Muskegon:** "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls" (Muskegon, 2022-09-07). Boat fishing was rated below average, with fish 55–100 ft down in 100–200 ft of water (Muskegon, 2022-09-14).
- **Rivers and Muskegon Lake:** I found no recent salmon reports for the river ports. The one Muskegon Lake mention was boat anglers catching a few salmon near the sand docks (Muskegon, 2022-09-14).

**Water and weather**
- The live feed wasn't available. I only have last week's buoy averages. Surface water was about 70–71 F at all four ports, with no sharp drop (St. Joseph 70 F, South Haven 71 F, Grand Haven and Muskegon 71 F).
- I have no modeled pierhead temperatures and no wind forecast, so I can't say whether an upwelling is coming.
- The last sharp drops were the week of 2022-08-17, when the buoys showed possible upwelling. Pier catches were still only "a few" then (Grand Haven and St. Joseph, 2022-08-17).

**My read**
- Surface water around 70 F is well above the 52–58 F range that Chinook and coho prefer (general guidance, NY DEC). I'd expect salmon to stay in deep, cooler water offshore, as the boat reports suggest.
- Michigan Sea Grant guidance says north or east winds can trigger an upwelling that pulls salmon toward pierheads. I'd expect pier fishing to improve only if one of those wind events happens.
- St. Joseph edges out the others because it has the only report of salmon at the pier heads. It still looks like a few fish at best.
- If you go, watch the buoy temperature and wind direction first. A sharp temperature drop would be your signal to fish the pier. Fish at first or last light. Cast spoons or fish spinners. These were the only pier-caught salmon lures mentioned (St. Joseph, 2022-08-17). Glow spoons were also used at Grand Haven (2022-08-17).

**Caveats**
- The reports are 6 days old, and the database only returned 2022 data. I couldn't compare against earlier seasons.
- The ratings are my judgment. Pier reports are sparse, and the boat reports show where the fish are, not how the piers will fish.
